Participant C suggested that the topic data could be used to populate a topic popup window.

A suggests improving search efficiency by making the search system return results only when necessary and when the user has a specific intent, reducing unnecessary loading time.
B agrees that users do not want to incur extra loading time if it can be avoided.

A asks about document frequency (DF) and whether it is needed for topic labeling.
B questions whether document frequencies are actually needed for the current task.
A confirms that document frequencies are needed for topic labeling.
B states that someone (@'s) was working on a related tool on Friday, which had document frequency data but had issues with proper functionality and was not working as intended.
A suggests that search functionality can be improved without TF-IDF, but that ranking results would be lost.
A explains that TF-IDF stands for Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency, and that it measures how often a term appears in a document and how rare it is across the entire corpus
C asks what TF-IDF stands for, and A provides a definition.
C asks what the general score in TF-IDF would represent, and A clarifies it is based on the entire corpus.
C suggests that having general frequencies would be useful, and A agrees.
A states that without a stop list, the search would be less effective, and that the system would assign a baseline score to non-relevant terms.
C asks what would happen if the system had fake topics or keyword lists, and A suggests a simple list of 3–5 key words would be the easiest approach.
A suggests that keyword search could be used as a topic search, allowing users to search for key terms instead of full text.
C agrees that a keyword list would be useful and would allow testing against hand-annotated data.
A states that calculating TF-IDF per topic would be too computationally expensive, and it's easier to calculate frequencies based on the whole corpus.
C agrees that calculating TF-IDF per topic would be difficult and not worth the effort.
A clarifies that search can be performed without TF-IDF, but results will not be ranked, and the system will not be able to distinguish relevance.
